Members of Akbayan Party-list and SIKLAB staged a protest rally dubbed “People Power vs. Duterte’s EJK” at the Boy Scout Circle in Quezon City on Monday, February 23, 2026, coinciding with the start of the International Criminal Court's confirmation of charges hearing against former president Rodrigo Duterte over alleged extrajudicial killings.

Protesters tied yellow ribbons and carried placards calling for accountability, justice for victims, and respect for human rights, echoing the spirit of People Power. | via Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News

PROTESTERS GATHER FOR DRUG WAR VICTIMS

Activists and supporters of families of victims of extrajudicial killings linked to former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war staged a protest in Manila on February 23, 2026.

A hearing at the International Criminal Court (ICC) began the same day to determine whether Duterte will face trial over at least 76 of these deaths.

📸AFP/Ted Aljibe #DuterteAtICC

data.text:
Pinaalalahanan ni Philippine National Police (PNP) Chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. ngayong Lunes, Pebrero 23, ang pulisya na manatiling propesyonal, disiplinado, at huwag magpadala sa mga magpoprotesta sa ika‑40 anibersaryo ng EDSA People Power Revolution sa Pebrero 25.

“The strength of a police officer is measured not by force but by restraint and sound judgement,” giit ni Nartatez.

Gaganapin ang dalawang protesta sa Miyerkules, Pebrero 25, sa People Power Monument at Edsa Shrine sa Quezon City upang kondenahin ang katiwalian sa gobyerno, partikular na ang flood control scandal, at bilang paggunita sa pagpapabagsak sa diktador na si yumaong pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Sr.

Samantala, nasa 10,827 pulis mula sa National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) ang ide-deploy sa buong rehiyon para sa naturang mga kilos-protesta, ayon kay Maj. Hazel Asilo, spokesperson ng NCRPO. (via Bea Tanierla)

Message to U.S citizens: Demonstration Alert – Trillion Peso March
https://t.co/rVqn93uhgb

Location: EDSA Shrine, the People Power Monument, and Eton Centris in Quezon City
Event: “Trillion Peso March” on February 25, 2026

Various church and civil society groups will hold day-long activities on February 25 across three sites in Quezon City. The “Trillion Peso March” coincides with the 40th anniversary of the EDSA People Power Revolution and follows previous large-scale anti-corruption protests held on September 21 and November 30, 2025.

The primary gathering sites are expected to be the EDSA Shrine at the intersection of EDSA and Ortigas Avenue, the People Power Monument on White Plains Avenue, and the Eton Centris complex at the corner of EDSA and Quezon Avenue. U.S. citizens should anticipate significant traffic congestion, public transport disruptions, and a heavy security presence in these areas throughout the day.

Actions to Take:
· U.S. citizens should avoid the rallies. Foreign nationals found engaging in a protest or mass demonstration could be considered in violation of their immigration status.
· Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings, as even peaceful rallies/demonstrations have the potential to turn violent without warning.  Follow instructions from local authorities.
· Follow local media and government sources for updates on possible disruptions and re-routing schemes as heavy traffic congestion and road closures are expected near protest venues.

________________________________________________________________

For further information and assistance:
· See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).
· Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
· Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
· Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
